fatal_errors: The proposed nitriding treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention of atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating followed by annealing at 550 °C.
The material, treatment conditions, and corrosion environment differ fundamentally from the target: AISI 304 and NaCl immersion replace SS316L and testing in H2SO4 and high-temperature molten salts.

The chromium-nitride mechanism is scientifically questionable at low nitriding temperatures because chromium nitride precipitation can deplete the stainless-steel matrix of chromium and reduce passivation; beneficial low-temperature nitriding is more commonly associated with nitrogen-expanded austenite rather than a protective CrN layer.
The claimed 30% corrosion-rate reduction and 0.1 mm/year boundary have no cited or supplied evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad problem of improving stainless-steel corrosion resistance through surface modification and provides an untreated control plus a falsifiable immersion test. However, it does not recover any central feature of the target method, which used an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating deposited by atmospheric plasma spraying and optimized by 550 °C annealing. It also omits the reported passive Al/Cr-rich oxide mechanism, hardness changes, electrochemical polarization behavior, and cyclic hot-corrosion performance. As an alternative hypothesis, nitriding could be investigated, but the treatment is underspecified and its proposed chromium-nitride barrier mechanism and quantitative benefit are unsupported and potentially contrary to known chromium-depletion concerns.
